sections.title: Issue 1 — SH2B3 EUR SuSiE-RSS re-fits (D-TA-02 + HQ#2(ii) headline)
sections.description: Three of five SH2B3 EUR per-trait SuSiE-RSS fits are non-converged at L=10 / niter=100 (the SuSiE iteration-cap regime per Wang et al. 2020 §Discussion); identity-LD hypertension carries L_saturated=TRUE in the per-fit JSON. Audit-V2 §HQ#2(i) marked this DEFERRED-COMPUTE pending an LSF slot — this phase fires it. Audit-V2 §HQ#2(ii) marked the headline-numerator question DEFERRED-DESIGN: when L=20 lands, do we recompute the 51/96 numerator (drop 18 non-converged → 33/96) or keep 51/96 with caveat? Plan must NOT pre-commit to a branch.

questions.title: L value for SH2B3 EUR per-trait re-fits (D-TA-02)
questions.context: Zou et al. 2022 §Discussion recommend setting L generously above the expected number of effects, then verifying n_CS << L. Compute envelope per audit-response: ~2–4 hours wall time on serial queue with la_multitrait_r env at L=20 (3-trait sweep). L-sweep {15, 20, 30} = ~9× compute over L=10 baseline.

options.label: L=20 single-shot (Zou 2022 default; ~3× compute over L=10)
options.description: Simplest: re-fit BMI/HTN/stroke at L=20 once, verify n_CS << L (e.g., n_CS ≤ 10). If any fit returns n_CS = 20 (saturation), Wave 1 escalates to L=30 within the same wave. Risk: if L=20 saturates, an extra LSF round-trip is needed.

options.label: L-sweep {15, 20, 30} pre-registered supplementary (recommended; ~9× compute)
options.description: Already pre-registered as a follow-on supplementary analysis. Three-point sensitivity sweep produces explicit evidence that n_CS plateaus and is robust to L choice. Generates a Supplementary Methods table the way Zou 2022 recommends. Burns ~12-15 hr LSF total but eliminates ambiguity. RECOMMENDED if OSF pre-reg already covers (verify D-TA-05).

options.label: L=20 with conditional-extension to L=30 if n_CS == L (saturation indicator)
options.description: Hybrid: start at L=20; if any of BMI/HTN/stroke returns n_CS = 20, fire that trait at L=30 in the same wave. Compute scales with saturation rate (~3× to ~6× compute). Rigorous AND adaptive.

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., L=20 single-shot now + L-sweep deferred to a separate Phase if needed; or L=30 single-shot to skip the sweep.

questions.title: Headline numerator decision when L=20 lands (HQ#2(ii) DEFERRED-DESIGN)
questions.context: Currently the manuscript's 51/96 yield headline pools the 18 non-converged fits with the 33 converged ones. Audit-V2 Eval 2(a) flagged this as 'non-convergence treated as data'. If L=20 converges some/all of the 18 non-converged, the numerator changes; if it doesn't, the question is whether to drop them from the headline. Materially shifts Abstract / Results §Headline / Fig 2 / TRACK-A-FROZEN-NUMBERS.md LIVE block.

options.label: Decide post-Wave-1 from observed convergence outcome (recommended)
options.description: Don't pre-commit. After Wave 1 produces the L=20 (or L-sweep) results, the empirical convergence rate dictates: if all 3 SH2B3 EUR traits converge, recompute 51/96 → (51+converged)/96; if some still don't converge, surface as a separate disclosure column. RECOMMENDED — outcome-driven, matches the honest-framing-lock principle of disk-then-narrative.

options.label: Keep 51/96 with caveat in place (don't recompute regardless of L=20 outcome)
options.description: Conservative: preserve byte-identical 51/96 throughout. Add a Limitations bullet stating 'the 51/96 yield includes 18 non-converged fits (3 of 5 at SH2B3 EUR); under L=20 these {converge / remain non-converged}'. Lowest manuscript-edit footprint; least responsive to new evidence.

options.label: Drop non-converged fits from numerator regardless (prefer the stricter denominator)
options.description: Most rigorous: numerator = converged-fits-with-non-empty-CS (e.g., 33/96 baseline; updated to (33 + Wave-1 converged)/96 post-fire). Stricter, smaller number, more defensible at peer review. But requires updating Abstract + Headline + Fig 2 caption + TRACK-A-FROZEN-NUMBERS.md LIVE block in Wave 6.

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., dual reporting: keep 51/96 as 'all-attempts' headline + add 33/96 as 'converged-only' Supplementary Methods column.

sections.title: Issue 1 — Canonical-pair coloc.susie scope (D-TA-03 + Wave 3 gate)
sections.description: The manuscript's canonical claims (PP.H4 = 1.00 at rs3184504, rs10774625, rs7137828, rs4766578 for BMI–hypertension and hypertension–stroke under Stage 1d identity-LD) have never been tested under reference-LD. Table 3 currently shows those rows as 'not executed'. Wave 2 fires coloc.susie on the chosen pairs against the Wave-1 converged fits; Wave 3 is the human-verify gate where Carter selects an honest 3-branch outcome (collapse / partial / survive).

questions.title: Canonical-pair coloc.susie scope (D-TA-03)
questions.context: Already on disk: SH2B3_12q24__EUR__asthma_vs_t2d (1 pair). Full SH2B3 EUR trait-pair lattice = 10 pairs (5 traits choose 2). FTO_16q12 EUR has all 10 pairs in the Stage 2 manifest — that's the symmetry target.

options.label: MINIMUM — BMI–HTN + HTN–stroke (2 new pairs; tests just the canonical literature claims)
options.description: Smallest scope; directly tests the rs3184504/rs10774625/rs7137828/rs4766578 PP.H4=1.00 claims; ~2× the LSF compute of Wave 2. Disadvantage: Table 3 SH2B3 row remains asymmetric vs FTO_16q12 (3/10 pairs filled vs 10/10). Reviewer may ask 'why only these two?'

options.label: RECOMMENDED — 9 new pairs (full SH2B3 EUR trait-pair lattice minus already-on-disk asthma-t2d)
options.description: asthma–bmi, asthma–hypertension, asthma–stroke, bmi–hypertension, bmi–stroke, bmi–t2d, hypertension–stroke, hypertension–t2d, stroke–t2d. Symmetrizes Table 3 SH2B3 row with FTO_16q12. ~9× the LSF compute of Wave 2 single pair. Gives a complete pleiotropy lattice for the flagship locus. RECOMMENDED.

options.label: MAXIMUM — 9 SH2B3 EUR + replicate 3-4 other regions against post-L=20 fits (cross-region consistency)
options.description: Adds FTO_16q12 EUR + MC4R_18q21 EUR + APOE_19q13 + CXADR_F2RL1_6p21 cross-region replication if their per-trait fits also benefit from L=20. Over-scopes the manuscript ask; pushes total compute to ~25× single-pair. Probably out of phase scope (would itself become a separate Phase).

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., MINIMUM at Wave 2 + 9-pair fill in a follow-on Phase; or 9 SH2B3 + ONLY FTO_16q12 EUR for cross-region check.

questions.title: PP.H4 outcome-branch threshold for Wave 3 human-verify gate
questions.context: Wave 3 is checkpoint:human-verify — Carter picks the SH2B3 outcome branch from observed disk numbers BEFORE narrative writes. The manuscript currently uses Tier B = 0.5 and Tier A = 0.8 throughout (per AUDIT-RESPONSE TRACK-A-FROZEN-NUMBERS L143 'Threshold preservation'). Lowering thresholds to surface the FTO Tier-C 0.3099 signal was rejected as out of scope during quick-260427-e8n. Wave 3 thresholds should match.

options.label: Standard manuscript thresholds (recommended): collapse <0.5 / partial 0.5–0.8 / survive ≥0.8
options.description: Preserves the manuscript's existing Tier B = 0.5 / Tier A = 0.8 thresholds verbatim. No OSF amendment needed. RECOMMENDED for consistency with the rest of the paper.

options.label: Lower bar — collapse <0.3 / partial 0.3–0.7 / survive ≥0.7
options.description: More permissive 'survive' gate. Surfaces sub-Tier-A signals as 'survives' (e.g., FTO_16q12 EUR at 0.3099 would count as 'partial'). Requires OSF amendment because thresholds shift. Disadvantage: changes the manuscript's threshold framing globally.

options.label: Higher bar — collapse <0.5 / partial 0.5–0.95 / survive ≥0.95
options.description: Stricter 'survive' gate matching the original PP.H4 = 1.00 identity-LD claim. Tests whether the canonical claim REALLY holds at near-perfect colocalization under matched-LD. Strongest finding under (a) collapse and (c) survive branches.

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., a 5-tier gate; or branch on the magnitude of PP.H4 drop relative to identity-LD's 1.00.

sections.title: Issue 2 — Variant-ID cache propagation refresh (D-TA-04)
sections.description: Code fixes 069b34f (run_qtl_coloc.R chr:pos tolerance) + 7d54183 (run_susie_rss.R LD-panel-rsid override) are committed in current branch but intermediate caches were generated before the commits and weren't invalidated. 1,005 / 1,274 (78.9 %) QTL-coloc attempts returned too_few_snps. Wave-0 diagnostic: read 3 SuSiE-RSS fit JSONs at results/fine_mapping/susie/*.json — chr:pos format → both layers stale; rsid format → QTL-coloc only.

questions.title: Cache-layer scope for Issue 2 re-fire (D-TA-04)
questions.context: QTL-coloc compute envelope: ~1,274 attempts × ~30 sec ≈ ~10 hr at 50 cores LSF. SuSiE-RSS layer adds ~5 hr if needed. PASS criterion: too_few_snps drops materially from 1,005 (target ≤200; success + no_qtl_cs counts rise). FAIL criterion: too_few_snps stays ~1,000 → SuSiE-RSS layer was the actual problem; root-cause investigation triggered, do NOT proceed to Wave 6.

options.label: DIAGNOSTIC-DRIVEN (recommended) — Wave 0 picks; Wave 4 scope decided by SuSiE-RSS variant-ID format check
options.description: Wave 0 reads 3 SuSiE-RSS JSONs to determine variant-ID format. If rsid: QTL-coloc only re-fire (~10 hr). If chr:pos: both layers re-fire (~15 hr total). Most efficient — only does work that's needed. RECOMMENDED. Plan PLAN.md must include both code paths and an explicit Wave-0 diagnostic gate.

options.label: CONSERVATIVE-BOTH — re-fire both layers regardless to eliminate cache-staleness as a confounder (~15 hr total)
options.description: Most defensible at peer review: 'we invalidated all caches between code-commits and re-fired everything'. Costs ~5 hr extra LSF. Eliminates any latent staleness in any cache. Lower risk of needing a Wave 4.5 fallback. Recommend if SuSiE-RSS Wave 0 diagnostic is ambiguous (e.g., mixed-format JSONs).

options.label: FAST-QTL-ONLY — re-fire only QTL-coloc; if Wave 4 verification fails, fall back to a Wave 4.5 SuSiE-RSS re-fire
options.description: Smallest critical-path commitment (~10 hr at 50 cores). Acceptable if Wave-0 diagnostic clearly shows rsid-format SuSiE-RSS JSONs (post-7d54183). Disadvantage: Wave 4 PASS criterion failure (~1,000 too_few_snps) triggers root-cause + Wave 4.5 re-fire (effectively conservative-both with extra round-trip).

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., re-fire QTL-coloc + a sample of 10 SuSiE-RSS fits in parallel as a Wave-4 verification sample.

sections.title: OSF pre-registration coverage (D-TA-05)
sections.description: Verify against osf.io/pvb5j (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/PVB5J) + closeout PDF at osf.io/az52u that the chosen D-TA-02 (L value) + D-TA-03 (canonical-pair scope) + D-TA-04 (cache scope) are pre-registered or covered by an existing amendment. The audit-response says the canonical-pair re-fire is 'pre-registered in TRACK-A-FROZEN-NUMBERS.md' — but verify that text is in OSF-deposited Methods, not only in the in-tree submission-bundle draft.

questions.title: OSF coverage for D-TA-02 (L value) + D-TA-03 (canonical-pair scope)
questions.context: Methods §Fine-Mapping Configuration in track_a_pivot.md states 'an L-sweep re-fit at L ∈ {15, 20, 30} is pre-registered as a follow-on supplementary analysis'. AUDIT-RESPONSE 2026-04-26 line 269 says HQ#2(iii) is 'pre-registered in TRACK-A-FROZEN-NUMBERS.md'. Both need OSF-portal verification (the in-tree draft is not the same as the OSF-deposited record).

options.label: Wave 0 verifies, then proceeds (recommended if pre-reg already covers)
options.description: Wave 0 task: ssh login02 (or equivalent); review osf.io/pvb5j Methods text + osf.io/az52u closeout PDF; confirm L-sweep wording + canonical-pair scope are present. If covered: proceed to Wave 1. If not covered: pause and Carter posts amendment. RECOMMENDED — saves a round-trip if pre-reg is sufficient.

options.label: Post OSF amendment NOW before any Wave 1 fire (Carter on OSF portal, ~30 min)
options.description: Defensive: post a pre-emptive amendment covering L value choice (whichever is selected in Q-02) + canonical-pair scope (whichever in Q-04) + cache invalidation (Q-08) BEFORE Wave 1 fires. ~30 min Carter web-UI action; rides on the existing osf.io/az52u closeout PDF as an addendum. Eliminates pre-reg risk entirely.

options.label: Defer the OSF check entirely until Wave 1 has produced results
options.description: Risky: if pre-reg doesn't cover and Wave 1 already fired, the amendment becomes retroactive. Not recommended. Pick only if Carter is confident pre-reg already fully covers all three sub-decisions.

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., split: verify L-sweep wording in OSF deposit (likely covered) + post amendment for canonical-pair scope only.

questions.title: OSF treatment of cache invalidation re-fire (D-TA-04)
questions.context: Cache invalidation re-fires with the SAME code (069b34f + 7d54183) + SAME data + SAME params — only the cache state changes. This is methodologically a 'cache hygiene fix', not a new analysis. Per Carter's command-args, this 'should be a deviation-log entry, NOT a pre-reg amendment'.

options.label: Deviation-log entry only (recommended; appended to .planning/amendments/osf_deviations.md or osf.io/az52u closeout addendum)
options.description: Methodologically correct: this is not a new analysis, it's a cache hygiene fix that produces the analysis the pre-reg already covers. Document the discovery + invalidation rationale + before/after numerics in the deviation log. RECOMMENDED.

options.label: Pre-reg amendment via osf.io/pvb5j (treat as new analysis)
options.description: Conservative: amend the pre-registration to explicitly cover the cache-invalidation re-fire. ~30 min Carter web-UI. Over-rigorous; cache hygiene fixes don't typically require pre-reg amendments. Pick only if Carter wants belt-and-suspenders.

options.label: Both — deviation-log entry + brief pre-reg amendment note
options.description: Maximum traceability. Costs an OSF round-trip but produces the most defensible audit trail.

options.label: Other (specify in chat_more)
options.description: E.g., deviation-log entry now + a single combined 'R2 amendment' covering all three D-TA-02/03/04 decisions in one OSF post.

The rename + reference-fix-up is non-trivial (~30-60 min Wave 6 task with grep+sed+verify md5 round-trip).

options.label: YES — rename to docs/manuscript/id-vs-ref-LD.md (recommended)
